statement: TACC's Horizon supercomputer at UT Austin is built around roughly 4,000 Blackwell-generation NVIDIA GPUs (stated as 4,032), paired with 2,000 Grace CPU nodes and 800 GB/sec InfiniBand.
why: A named academic buildout of this size shows Blackwell-class merchant GPUs winning FP64-sensitive scientific workloads, a segment outside the usual hyperscaler and neocloud demand base.

impact.mechanism: An academic HPC centre standardising on Blackwell GPUs with Grace CPUs and InfiniBand fabric commits several thousand accelerators and matching network capacity to a single vendor's platform.

evidence.excerpt: will have around 4,000 GPUs. (The number is actually 4,032, despite what the chart above says.)
expected startup in spring 2026, with full production expected by summer 2026

confidence.basis: Single secondary outlet, published 2025-11-25 and so more than nine months stale relative to this run; the document notes no TACC or NVIDIA release closer to the present could be located to confirm delivery.

dispersion: GPU count given as around 4,000 in the chart but 4,032 in the text; the specific Blackwell variant is inferred (B200 likely per the article, NVL4 per other cited materials), not confirmed.
entity: TACC (Texas Advanced Computing Center) / UT Austin
